subject: Geography
description: Forest types, distribution, conservation, key tribes/species

questions.stem: India's TOTAL FOREST + tree cover is approximately what percent of geographical area?
questions.explanation: India's forest + tree cover (per India State of Forest Report 2023, FSI-MoEFCC): ~25.17% of total geographic area (forest cover ~21.7% + tree cover ~3.4%). NATIONAL FOREST POLICY 1988 TARGET: 33% (66% in hilly areas) — STILL UNMET after 35+ years. Top 5 forest-cover states by AREA: Madhya Pradesh > Arunachal Pradesh > Chhattisgarh > Odisha > Maharashtra. By PERCENTAGE OF AREA: Mizoram (highest, ~85%), Lakshadweep, A&N Islands, Arunachal Pradesh. Concerns: deforestation, tribal land rights (Forest Rights Act 2006), encroachment, mining. CO₂ ABSORPTION: forests absorb ~12% of India's emissions; key for climate goals (Paris commitment: 2.5-3 BtCO₂e additional sink by 2030).

questions.stem: TROPICAL EVERGREEN forests of India are mainly found in:
questions.explanation: TROPICAL EVERGREEN — heavy rainfall (>200 cm), high temp + humidity. Multi-storied dense canopy; trees never shed all leaves at once. Areas: WESTERN GHATS (Kerala, southern Karnataka, Maharashtra, Goa); ANDAMAN + NICOBAR; NE INDIA (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal). KEY species: rosewood, mahogany, ebony, rubber, cinchona. Has 'wet evergreen' + 'semi-evergreen' subtypes. FOREST TYPES IN INDIA (Champion + Seth classification, 1968): (1) Tropical Evergreen + Semi-Evergreen; (2) Tropical Deciduous (LARGEST area — Sal, Teak); (3) Tropical Thorn / Scrub (arid Rajasthan); (4) Tidal / Mangrove (Sundarbans, Kutch coast); (5) Montane (Himalayan — sub-tropical, temperate, alpine). Each adapted to climate.

questions.stem: TEAK + SAL trees are found in which forest type?
questions.explanation: TROPICAL DECIDUOUS (MONSOON) FORESTS — India's MOST EXTENSIVE forest type (~38% of forest cover). Trees SHED leaves in dry season (winter / hot summer) to conserve water — adaptation to monsoon climate. RAINFALL: 70-200 cm/year. KEY SPECIES: TEAK (Tectona grandis) — premium timber, MP-Maharashtra; SAL (Shorea robusta) — Eastern + Central India; SANDALWOOD (Karnataka — state tree); BAMBOO; mahua, neem, sissoo, arjun, palash. SUBTYPES: MOIST DECIDUOUS (100-200 cm rain — TEAK) + DRY DECIDUOUS (70-100 cm — SAL). HUGE economic value: timber, fuel, bamboo, lac, gum, herbs. STATES: MP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha — major teak/sal regions. FAST FACT: SAL is the dominant tree of Jharkhand + state tree of Chhattisgarh; TEAK is state tree of Maharashtra.

questions.stem: CHIPKO MOVEMENT (1973), to protect forests by HUGGING trees, started in:
questions.explanation: CHIPKO ('to embrace') — 26 March 1974, RENI VILLAGE (Chamoli, Uttarakhand). Women led by GAURA DEVI hugged trees to prevent loggers from cutting. Sparked nationwide environmental movement. KEY LEADERS: SUNDERLAL BAHUGUNA (Padma Vibhushan; coined 'ECOLOGY = PERMANENT ECONOMY'), CHANDI PRASAD BHATT (Magsaysay Award 1982). RESULT: 1980 BAN on commercial felling above 1000 m altitude in UP for 15 years. PRECURSOR: BISHNOI movement (1730, Khejarli, Rajasthan — Amrita Devi + 363 villagers killed protecting Khejri trees). LATER: APPIKO movement (1983, Karnataka — same idea in Western Ghats). NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (Medha Patkar, 1985+). India has rich tradition of grassroots environmentalism.

questions.stem: NILGIRI BIOSPHERE RESERVE, India's first such reserve (1986), is in:
questions.explanation: NILGIRI BIOSPHERE RESERVE — India's FIRST biosphere reserve, designated 1986. Spans TAMIL NADU + KARNATAKA + KERALA tri-junction. Includes: MUDUMALAI (TN) + BANDIPUR (KAR) + WAYANAD (KER) + NAGARHOLE (KAR) + SILENT VALLEY NP (KER). Home to: ELEPHANTS, TIGERS, GAUR, INDIAN BISON, NILGIRI TAHR (state animal of TN), nilgiri langur, hornbills. UNESCO MAB Network member 2000. INDIA has 18 BIOSPHERE RESERVES (12 part of UNESCO MAB Network). OTHER notable: Sundarbans (1989; UNESCO 2001 — saltwater crocodiles, tigers); Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand); Gulf of Mannar (TN); Pachmarhi (MP); Nokrek (Meghalaya); Manas (Assam); Kachchh, Cold Desert (HP), Khangchendzonga (Sikkim).

questions.stem: WHICH state has the LARGEST FOREST AREA (in absolute sq km)?
questions.explanation: MADHYA PRADESH — largest STATE forest area (~77,500 sq km). Reasons: large state size + Vindhya/Satpura hill ranges + sal-teak forests. Rank by AREA (sq km): MP > Arunachal > Chhattisgarh > Odisha > Maharashtra. Rank by PERCENTAGE: Mizoram (~85%) > Lakshadweep > A&N > Arunachal > Meghalaya. CRITIC: MP has lost some forest lately (mining, infrastructure); Mizoram has highest % but its absolute area is small. NATIONAL PARKS: India has 106 (latest count). MP alone has 11 NPs (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura — 'TIGER STATE' of India). FOREST POLICY 1988 set 33% target — far from achieved (~25%); main barriers = land hunger, mining demand, encroachment.

questions.stem: PROJECT TIGER (1973) was launched at which national park first?

options.option_text: Kanha NP, in Madhya Pradesh here
Bandhavgarh NP, in MP also here

questions.explanation: PROJECT TIGER — launched 1 April 1973 at JIM CORBETT NATIONAL PARK (Uttarakhand) — also India's FIRST national park (1936, originally 'Hailey NP', renamed Jim Corbett 1957 after the British hunter-conservationist who saved Bengal tigers). INITIAL: 9 reserves, 268 tigers (1973 census). NOW: 55 tiger reserves, ~3682 tigers (2022 census — about 75% of world tiger population!). Indian govt's flagship conservation programme. NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) since 2006. STATE WITH MOST TIGERS: Madhya Pradesh (~785 tigers) > Karnataka > Uttarakhand. Other ICONIC species programmes: PROJECT ELEPHANT (1992), PROJECT CHEETAH (2022 — 8 + 12 cheetahs from Namibia + S Africa to Kuno NP MP — first inter-continental large carnivore translocation), Project DOLPHIN, Hangul, etc.
